title: Inter-team Dependency Handshake & Readiness Badging
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem: Cross-team handoffs frequently surface late blockers during rollout windows because dependency status is represented as free-text notes in tickets or stale spreadsheets. We need a lightweight operational contract that teams can accept and an at-a-glance readiness badge visible on roadmap views and initiative pages.

Goal: Create an inter-team 'handshake' protocol that formalizes minimal acceptance criteria per dependency, embeds a 3-state readiness badge (Not Ready / Ready with Conditions / Ready), and wires automated nudges and escalations when readiness doesn't progress before cutover windows.

Out of scope: Full enforcement of SLAs, replacing existing ownership model, or building a global dependency solver. This is a pragmatic, UX-forward rollout that complements existing interlock runbooks.

Key deliverables:
- Readiness schema (fields + minimal acceptance checklist) that teams can attach to PM/ENG/DES issues.
- Visual badge component in Console roadmap and initiative pages.
- Server-side evaluator that computes badge state from checklists + last-updated timestamp.
- Nudge automation (Slack/email) and an on-call escalation path after configurable windows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Schema defined and documented in Confluence with examples for Eng, Design, Security, and Infra dependencies.
2) Console shows badge on initiative detail and roadmap lane; clicking badge opens the checklist modal.
3) At least two teams (Infra and Eng) onboard with checklists for a pilot initiative.
4) Nudges trigger when a dependency remains in Not Ready for 5 business days pre-cutover; escalation to PM and project lead occurs after 2 missed nudges.
5) Dashboards show coverage (% of open dependencies with badges) and mean time from "Not Ready" to "Ready" for pilot projects.
success_metrics: Coverage: >= 75% of cross-team dependencies in pilot have badges by pilot end
Blocker reduction: 30% fewer last-minute cutover blockers vs previous quarter
Time-to-ready: median "Not Ready" -> "Ready" under 10 days for pilot
